name.text: Calculating disjoint probabilities and inverse cumulative temperatures for a uniform distribution

questiontext.text:
The daily high temperature (\(T\)) in Kisumu during July is uniformly distributed between {@a@}\(^{\circ}\text{C}\) and {@b@}\(^{\circ}\text{C}\).

a) Calculate the probability that on a randomly selected day, the high temperature is either less than {@c@}\(^{\circ}\text{C}\) OR greater than {@d@}\(^{\circ}\text{C}\).

(Enter your answer as a fully simplified fraction).

\(P =\) [[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

b) A meteorologist states that the probability of the temperature being less than or equal to a specific unknown temperature \(t\) is exactly \({@target_prob_tex@}\).

Use the cumulative distribution formula to find the exact temperature \(t\).

\(t =\) [[input:ans2]] \(^{\circ}\text{C}\)

[[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

Part a: Disjoint Probabilities
The total width of our uniform distribution is \(b - a = {@b@} - {@a@} = {@w@}\).

Because the events "less than {@c@}" and "greater than {@d@}" do not overlap (they are mutually exclusive), we calculate their probabilities separately and add them together:

\( \displaystyle P(T < {@c@}) = \frac{{@c@} - {@a@}}{{@w@}} = \frac{{@c - a@}}{{@w@}} \)

\( \displaystyle P(T > {@d@}) = \frac{{@b@} - {@d@}}{{@w@}} = \frac{{@b - d@}}{{@w@}} \)

\( \displaystyle P(T < {@c@} \text{ or } T > {@d@}) = \frac{{@c - a@}}{{@w@}} + \frac{{@b - d@}}{{@w@}} = \frac{{@c - a + b - d@}}{{@w@}} \)

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ P(\text{combined}) = {@ta1@} } \)

Part b: Inverse Cumulative Probability
We are given the cumulative probability \(P(T \le t) = {@target_prob_tex@}\). For a uniform distribution, the formula for cumulative probability is:

\( \displaystyle P(T \le t) = \frac{t - a}{b - a} \)

Substitute the known values into the formula and solve for \(t\):

\( \displaystyle \frac{t - {@a@}}{{@w@}} = {@target_prob_tex@} \)

\( \displaystyle t - {@a@} = {@target_prob_tex@} \times {@w@} \)

\( \displaystyle t - {@a@} = {@target_prob_num * w@} \)

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ t = {@ta2@} } \)

questionnote.text: U({@a@}, {@b@}). w={@w@}. P(T<{@c@} OR T>{@d@}) = {@ta1@}. Target P = {@target_prob_tex@}, t = {@ta2@}

This question is based on the examples Finding an Unknown Value from a Given Probability and Combining Probability Rules in the section Continuous Probability I of the CBC Grade 11 Mathematics textbook (INNODEMS).

Continuous Probability (Uniform Distribution)

node.description: Algebraic equivalence of disjoint probability sum

truefeedback.text: Correct. You successfully calculated the probabilities of both intervals and added them together.

node.description: Check if they multiplied instead of added

truefeedback.text: You multiplied the two probabilities together. Because the events are mutually exclusive (connected by "OR"), you must add their individual probabilities.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Calculate \(P(T < {@c@})\) and \(P(T > {@d@})\) separately, and then add those two fractions together.

truefeedback.text: Excellent. You successfully used the cumulative distribution formula to solve backwards for \(t\).

node.description: Check if they forgot to add the minimum temperature 'a'

truefeedback.text: You calculated the correct geometric width (\(t - a\)), but you forgot to add the starting temperature (\(a = {@a@}\)) back to your final answer to find the actual temperature \(t\).

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Set up the equation \(\frac{t - {@a@}}{{@w@}} = {@target_prob_tex@}\) and solve algebraically for \(t\).
